_about: What the template picker's details panel shows for each approved template (K, 2026-10-05: original size, player counts, underground on or off, and what makes the template unique). Keyed by the template's name, as in approved-templates.json. Facts come from the template's own file (src/rmg/templates); the description is written from its structure. Outside generator/, so editing it needs no re-pinning. Fields: originalSizeMin and originalSizeMax (tiles, one side), originalLevels (1 or 2; 2 means the original is a two-level template), playersMin and playersMax, humansMax, underground (a sentence), zones (total) and zonesByKind, description (plain text, paragraphs split by a blank line). original (an object): only the original game's own facts for the template, each confirmed by the online check of TEMPLATE-MATCHING-PLAYBOOK.md section 9 step 10, with its sources: players, humans, humanStartZones, computerStartZones, sizeMin and sizeMax (tiles, one side), sizeNames, levels, zones, zonesByKind, checked (date), source (a list of {what, url}), notChecked. The launcher's Original game specs box reads this block and nothing else; what OmniMapGen allows beyond it stays in the flat fields and the description. originalPreferences: the values the "original template preferences" switch sets (levers, templateChoices, ranges, modContent, leversWithNoEffectOnTemplates).

Coldshadow's Fantasy.underground: Two levels in the original; also plays on one level, with the underground zones gathered in the middle of the surface
Coldshadow's Fantasy.description:
An eight-player funnel. Every player starts in a large zone with a castle of their own and a short, guarded road to a treasure zone that has a neutral castle. Two such treasure zones meet at a junction, the junctions pair up, and all four open into one rich centre zone.

The four junction zones are the template's signature. Each lies underground (on a one-level map they gather in the middle of the surface) and holds a neutral dragon dwelling, the Crystal, Azure, Faerie and Rust dragons, behind strong guards. The centre zone has the richest treasure on the map, and every door into it is guarded for 60,000.

The original has two start zones for human players and six for computer players only, so it takes at most two human players, and one is allowed too. Each human start leaves by a road guarded three times as hard as a computer start does. OmniMapGen lets any number of players be human here, and a map with more players than the template has starts adds extra start zones of its own.

originalPreferences.about: What 'Restrict all settings to original template preferences' sets for this template: every lever at its template value (the default, which is the template's own 1x), every setting that offers a Template choice locked to it, size, players and humans inside the original's ranges. A lever listed in leversWithNoEffectOnTemplates is not measured to do anything on a template (LEVER-TABLE.md, after MapGen Dev's k23), so freezing it changes nothing that is known.

Classic.underground: One level or two, as the Underground setting says
Classic.description:
Start here if you are new to Heroes or to Dead Man's Boots. This is an ordinary random Heroes map: each player starts in a region of their own with mines close by, the treasure and the neutral towns lie in the regions between, and monsters guard the ways from one region to the next. It takes any size from Small to Giant and 2 to 8 players, on one level or two, and every setting starts at its default.

This is DMB's own Nostalgia: a random map in the spirit of Horn of the Abyss's Nostalgia, with a wide range of variability drawn from generic and original game and map ideas. It is the layout every other setting starts from, each at its Template value, which for this entry is the setting's own default. Random can pick it.

It has no template file and no fixed zones. The generator draws the biomes (the zones) of the map from the map size and the number of players. Each player gets a start biome, and the starts together take about half the land; the rest are treasure biomes, which carry the dear loot, and neutral town biomes. Biome size sets how many biomes there are, and Start biome size and Treasure biomes set their shares of the land.

How the biomes join is the Layout family setting: Mixed (neighbours as the map's cut makes them), Tree (one way between any two biomes), Sparse mesh (a tree with a few loops), Hub (every start joins one central biome), Pairs (the starts joined two by two), Ring (the biomes round the map's edge in a circle), Chain (that circle opened into a line) or Random (one of these, from the seed). Past Mixed, Biome connections opens more borders on top. Portal share turns that share of the links into portal pairs, and Passages with road and Passages without road decide which links carry a road.

Monsters stand in the ways between biomes (Guards at bottlenecks and Bottleneck guard share; a way out of a start always has one). Guard gradient makes the ways near the starts weaker and the farthest ones stronger, and Guards by distance does the same for every kind of guard, the stacks nearest the starts a creature level weaker and the farthest a level stronger. Guards on treasure, mines and dwellings, Monster count, Monster tier and Stack size set the rest.

Mines, dwellings, artifacts and loot follow Mines, Creature dwellings, Artifacts and Treasure biomes. Every setting on the other pages applies, and Reset sets each one to its Template value. Mini Nostalgia (approximate) and Nostalgia (approximate) are this layout with its sliders set toward the numbers of HotA's two templates.

Size, players and humans stay anywhere the generator allows. Mod content stays the player's own choice.

Random.underground: One level or two, as the Underground setting says
Random.description:
Random runs one of the templates in this list at random: Classic and every scenario template that takes the map's size, players and levels. The pick is made from the map's seed, so the same seed gives the same template, and the log line 'random: template ...' names it.

All the other settings read the picked template's own preferences when set to Template, which is what the Reset button sets.

originalPreferences.about: What the Reset button sets for Random: every lever at Template, so each is read from whichever template the seed picks; the values listed are the defaults, which is what Classic uses.

Mini Nostalgia (approximate).underground: One level at Large, two at Extra Large in the original; here one level or two, as the Underground setting says
Mini Nostalgia (approximate).description: APPROXIMATE. Mini Nostalgia is a small, typical Heroes map: 8 start zones and 7 treasure zones joined as a tree, the start zones holding two thirds of the land, guards at every link, ordinary monsters. This entry is not that template. It is the open layout (Classic) with the sliders that exist today set toward its numbers: big start biomes (Start biome size 0.65), about 14 zones at Biome size 400, many links as portals (Portal share 0.6), fewer guards (Monster count 0.3), fewer dear piles (Treasure biomes 0.1, Artifacts 0.002), fewer dwellings (Creature dwellings 0.7), the guard gradient at 1 and the Layout family at Tree. On a 108x108 map of 4 players it measures: zones 14 (the original 15), the start zones' share of the land 0.63 (0.66), links per zone 0.68 (0.65), portals 14 (8.7), guard stacks 12.3 per 1000 tiles (10.6), dear piles 7.0 per 1000 tiles (5.2). It gets closer as junction zones, wide links and a second town in a start zone are added to the generator. Any setting can still be changed.

Nostalgia (approximate).underground: Two levels in the original; here one level or two, as the Underground setting says
Nostalgia (approximate).description: APPROXIMATE. Nostalgia is a large, typical Heroes map: 8 start zones and 16 treasure zones joined as a mesh, a third of the land in the start zones, guards at every link, ordinary monsters. This entry is not that template. It is the open layout (Classic) with the sliders that exist today set toward its numbers: Biome size 1500 for about 22 zones, most links as portals (Portal share 0.8), fewer guards (Monster count 0.5), fewer dear piles (Treasure biomes 0.1, Artifacts 0.003), more dwellings (Creature dwellings 1.2), the guard gradient at 1 and the Layout family at Tree. On a 144x144 map of 4 players with two levels it measures: zones 22.5 (the original 24), the start zones' share of the land 0.31 (0.31), links per zone 0.75 (0.45), portals 29 (42.7), guard stacks 14.6 per 1000 tiles (13.6), dear piles 8.5 per 1000 tiles (6.3). The links stay above the original's because the map has 8 monolith channels, which limit how many links can be portal pairs. It gets closer as junction zones, wide links and a second town in a start zone are added to the generator. Any setting can still be changed.
